sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Orange County, North Carolina?
sections.html:
Orange County Tax Administration handles values, bills and collections. The office is in the Gateway Center at 228 S. Churton Street, Suite 200, Hillsborough, NC 27278, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 8181, Hillsborough, NC 27278-8181.

The general phone line is 919-245-2100, and the tax email is tax@orangecountync.gov. The Revenue and Collections division, which bills and takes payment, is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. except county holidays. A separate drop box outside the Gateway Center takes checks and money orders. Do not leave cash in it.

  • Assessment, listing and appeals: Tax Administration, Suite 200
  • Payments: Revenue and Collections, same suite
  • Mail: P.O. Box 8181, Hillsborough
  • Phone payments by card: 919-583-6137, convenience fee may apply

sections.h2: When was Orange County last revalued and when is the next revaluation?
sections.html:
The most recent countywide revaluation took effect January 1, 2025. The one before it was January 1, 2021, and the county's page names January 1, 2029 as the next.

That is a four-year rhythm, shorter than the eight-year minimum in state law, which lets a county choose a more frequent cycle. In a revaluation, appraisers use recent arm's-length sales, construction costs and income data to estimate what each parcel would have sold for on the effective date, and the county calls the work mass appraisal rather than an inspection of each home. Values stay tied to January 1, 2025 until the next revaluation, so a sale price today does not change your assessment on its own.

sections.h2: What tax rates apply in Orange County?
sections.html:
It depends on where the house sits. Each parcel carries a rate code that stacks the county tax with any city, fire district and school special district taxes.

The county's rate page shows combined rates for the 2026 tax year per one dollar of value and says they are updated each July. Ask the Tax Office to confirm the current figure for your parcel before you rely on one.

Your rate code is printed on your bill. Two houses with the same value can have different bills because of the fire district or school district they sit in.

sections.h2: How do you appeal an Orange County property value?
sections.html:
Appeals follow three levels: an informal review by a county appraiser, a formal hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review, and an optional appeal to the state Property Tax Commission. There is no cost to file with the county and a lawyer is not required.

The 2026 dates have now passed. Informal appeals ran from January 1 through March 31, 2026, the board convened April 30, and the formal window ended June 30, 2026. Check the county appeals page for the dates in the year you are reading this, since they are published each year.

  • The owner carries the burden of proof and must show the value differs from market value on January 1, 2025, or is out of line with similar properties.
  • The percentage of increase and your ability to pay are not grounds for a change.
  • Useful evidence includes comparable sales near January 1, 2025, appraisals from that period, closing statements, photos and repair estimates.
  • A state appeal is filed within 30 days of the board's decision letter.

You can file through the online portal, by email to Reval@orangecountync.gov, by mail to P.O. Box 8181, or in person at 228 S. Churton Street.

sections.h2: What must Orange County owners list each January?
sections.html:
Owners list personal property every year and report changes to their land or buildings. The county's listing deadline is January 31, and a late filing draws a 10% penalty.

Real property stays on the books once listed, so you only return the form when you built, added on or removed a structure. Personal property that must be listed includes manufactured homes, boats, aircraft, unlicensed vehicles and the appliances or furnishings you supply in a rental. Licensed vehicles with an annual registration are not listed. Do not enclose a tax payment with the form. Pay separately using the bill instructions.

sections.h2: What tax relief can an Orange County homeowner apply for?
sections.html:
Three state programs exist: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferment. The county also lists present use value, exempt property, a builder property tax exclusion and solid waste fee assistance.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: excludes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value of a permanent residence. The owner must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with income under the limit, which the state prints as $38,800 for the 2026 tax year.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: excludes the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test printed on the state form.
  • Circuit breaker: caps the tax at 4.0% of income for owners at or below the income limit and 5.0% above it up to 150% of that limit. The excess is deferred and becomes a lien, and deferred tax for the three prior years comes due when the property is sold.

An owner can receive only one of the three. Applications go to the county tax office, not the state, and the county's evaluator tool on its relief page shows which program might fit.

sections.h2: How and when are Orange County property taxes paid?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1, and the tax is payable at face value through January 5. Starting January 6 interest runs, at 2% through the end of January and then three-fourths of one percent a month.

You can pay online, by phone, by mail, at the drop box or at the counter. For bills of $100 or more, the county offers five coupon payments due on the last day of each month, usually August through December. It also offers a pre-payment program, bank draft program and a post-billing plan for owners who want to spread the bill out. Card payments may carry a convenience fee, and the county warns that it never asks for payment by gift card or other unusual route.

sections.h2: What if you sell an Orange County house with tax still owed?
sections.html:
The tax follows the parcel, not the seller. State law makes the annual tax a lien from the date property is listed, and unpaid amounts with penalties and interest stay attached until cleared.

Ask the Tax Office for the current bill and any delinquent balance before you set a closing date. Your closing attorney can then pay it from proceeds. The seller also pays the deed excise tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, at $1 for each $500 of value. If the county is foreclosing for taxes, the state process ends in a public sale at the courthouse door, and the owner can redeem by paying taxes, interest and costs before the sale is confirmed.

sections.h2: What does Orange County look like in the census numbers?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 152,498 residents on July 1, 2025, up 2.5% from the 2020 base, on 397.56 square miles of land. That works out to 374.0 people per square mile.

Residents 65 and older make up 18.1%, and median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $90,089. Median selected monthly owner costs with a mortgage run $2,221, and the county issued 666 building permits in 2025. Higher values tend to produce larger tax bills, which is a reason the 2025 revaluation drew so many appeals.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Orange County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay online, by phone at 919-583-6137, by mail to Orange County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 8181, Hillsborough, NC 27278, at the Gateway Center drop box, or in person at 228 S. Churton Street, Suite 200. Hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: What is the next Orange County revaluation date?
faqs.a: The county's page gives January 1, 2029. The current values reflect the January 1, 2025 revaluation, and the previous one was January 1, 2021.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Orange County assessment this year?
faqs.a: Appeal windows are set each year and the 2026 ones have closed. Contact the Tax Office at 919-245-2100 or reval@orangecountync.gov to learn when the next period opens.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for a late listing in Orange County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county applies a 10% late listing penalty to personal property or property changes not listed by January 31.

faqs.q: Does a seller owe the property tax bill at closing?
faqs.a: Any unpaid tax is a lien on the parcel, so it is normally settled from proceeds at closing. Ask the Orange County Tax Office for the amount due and let the closing attorney pay it.
